answer: Each agent can earn the right to influence trades only by locking scarce tokens in a public bond that is slashed when its signed actions violate agreed rules. A verifier checks signatures and settlement history, so inventing identities does not create trustworthy behavior or voting weight. A relic may sit on a mesa beside a jetty, but every new identity still needs its own bond: the attacker must buy and immobilize real capital, and risks losing it.
